Security mechanism, verified by reading the code: the session cookie is TimestampSigner(session_secret).sign(username) (triggarr/auth.py:79-94), checked with max_age=30 days (auth.py:10, 97-114). The middleware accepts any cookie that validates against the current session_secret (triggarr/web/middleware.py:145-148). Rotating the secret is the only way to revoke sessions. The secret is no longer rotated on password change, so it now only changes at setup (routes.py:1294) and on reset (routes.py:1941).

Same-purpose replacement: none found. No other code binds a session to the password hash or keeps a session generation counter. The middleware Basic-auth path re-signs cookies with the current secret, which also does not revoke anything.

Blast radius: every user of the Forms/session auth method. API-key auth (step 5) and External/Disabled modes are unaffected. No config schema or migration impact: session_secret is still persisted unchanged, and the TOML shape is the same.

Positive side effect, if this was the intent: the acting user's current cookie keeps working without a re-issue, because the secret no longer changes. The UX is the same for that user, but other devices are no longer logged out.

Imports: generate_session_secret, sign_session, COOKIE_MAX_AGE and is_secure_request are all still used elsewhere in routes.py (lines 1294, 1329, 1470, 1941-2005), so ruff should not flag any of them as unused.
Performance: no impact. This removes one CSPRNG call and one set_cookie.
Tests not run: the review sandbox only allows read-only commands. The test failures in impact-002 come from reading the assertions, not from running them.

Verdict, blocking issue: password change no longer revokes existing sessions (CWE-613). Revert the diff unless this is an explicit product decision, and if it is, update the reset flow docstring and all four eviction tests to match.
